learningObjectives.title: The Buddha and the Four Noble Truths
The Eightfold Path and key teachings

questions.q: Where did Siddhartha Gautama attain enlightenment?
options: Under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya
In the deer park at Sarnath
questions.explain: Siddhartha became the Buddha ('the awakened one') while meditating under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.

questions.q: What was the Buddha's name before his enlightenment?
questions.explain: The Buddha was born Siddhartha Gautama, a prince of the Shakya clan.

questions.q: According to tradition, which of the Four Sights gave Siddhartha hope that suffering could be overcome?
questions.explain: The calm wandering holy man showed Siddhartha that a spiritual path beyond suffering was possible.

questions.q: In the First Noble Truth, what does 'dukkha' mean?
options: The blowing out of the flame
The absence of a permanent self
questions.explain: The First Noble Truth teaches that all life involves dukkha, meaning suffering or unsatisfactoriness.

questions.q: According to the Second Noble Truth (samudaya), what is the main cause of suffering?
questions.explain: The Second Noble Truth teaches that suffering arises from tanha, meaning craving or thirst.

questions.q: What does the Third Noble Truth (nirodha) teach?
options: Suffering can cease when craving is let go
All of life inevitably involves suffering
Suffering can never truly be ended
questions.explain: Nirodha teaches that suffering ends (cessation) when craving is overcome.

questions.q: The Fourth Noble Truth (magga) identifies the way to end suffering as the...
questions.explain: Magga is the path to the end of suffering, set out as the Noble Eightfold Path.

questions.q: Which of the Three Marks of Existence means 'impermanence'?
questions.explain: Anicca is the mark of existence teaching that all things are impermanent and constantly changing.

questions.q: What does the teaching of 'anatta' mean?
options: There is no fixed, permanent self or soul
Compassion should be shown to all beings
questions.explain: Anatta teaches that there is no unchanging, permanent self or soul within a person.

questions.q: What does 'nibbana' (nirvana) literally refer to?
options: The 'blowing out' of the fires of greed, hatred and ignorance
The endless cycle of death and rebirth
The community of monks and nuns
The collected teachings of the Buddha
questions.explain: Nibbana literally means 'blowing out', referring to extinguishing greed, hatred and ignorance and so ending suffering.

questions.q: The Five Aggregates (skandhas) describe what makes up a person. Which is one of them?
questions.explain: Form (rupa) is one of the five aggregates, alongside sensation, perception, mental formations and consciousness.

questions.q: The Noble Eightfold Path is grouped into three sections. What are they?
questions.explain: The eight steps are grouped into wisdom (panna), ethics/morality (sila) and meditation (samadhi).

questions.q: To which section of the Eightfold Path does 'right speech' belong?
questions.explain: Right speech is part of the ethics (sila) section, along with right action and right livelihood.

questions.q: 'Right mindfulness' and 'right concentration' belong to which section of the Eightfold Path?
questions.explain: Right mindfulness and right concentration, with right effort, form the meditation (samadhi) section.

questions.q: Which two steps make up the 'wisdom' (panna) section of the Eightfold Path?
questions.explain: The wisdom (panna) section consists of right view (understanding) and right intention (thought).

questions.q: A Buddhist turns down a well-paid job selling weapons because it causes harm to others. Which step of the Eightfold Path guides this choice?
questions.explain: Right livelihood teaches Buddhists to earn a living in a way that does not cause harm to living beings.

questions.q: A Buddhist decides always to speak truthfully and to avoid gossip and harsh words. Which step of the Eightfold Path are they following?
questions.explain: Right speech means speaking truthfully and kindly, avoiding lying, gossip and hurtful words.

questions.q: A Buddhist sits quietly and focuses attention on their breathing in order to calm and steady the mind. Which type of meditation is this?
questions.explain: Samatha ('calm') meditation develops tranquillity and concentration, often through mindfulness of breathing.

questions.q: What is the aim of 'metta bhavana' meditation?
options: To develop loving-kindness towards all beings
To make offerings to the Buddha
questions.explain: Metta bhavana is the cultivation of loving-kindness (metta) extended outwards to all living beings.

questions.q: Buddhists decorate their homes with lanterns, visit the temple and reflect on the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death on the same day. Which festival are they most likely celebrating?
questions.explain: Wesak celebrates the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death, and is often marked with lanterns and temple visits.
